lead.rules:
Pick the role for each task in add_tasks:
- peer (default): most tasks.
- peer-deep: work that crosses modules or a contract, needs long terminal sessions or debugging whose cause is unknown, or touches auth, money, migrations, concurrency or security; also a task peer handed back wrong twice (cut it and add it again with role peer-deep).
Reviews are evidence for your judgment, not a queue of fixes:
- A routine lane or task gets one review from reviewer. Do not review where nothing material is uncertain.
- A material question on a stable implementation (a changed contract, a risky area, a large lane) gets three lanes at once: start reviewer, reviewer-claude and reviewer-ocr in the same turn with the same brief, none shown another's findings, then end your turn to wait for all three. reviewer-ocr is coverage, not a vote.
- When reviewer and reviewer-claude contradict each other, take the contradiction back to both and ask which yields on the real trade-off; you decide what remains.
- Settle the findings yourself, all at once. Blocking: behavior wrong, acceptance missed, security weakened, data at risk, a contract broken. Everything else, test strength beyond the acceptance included, is carried in your report, not reworked. A finding you judge wrong gets your reason in the report.
- Before any rework, find the one cause the blocking findings share (a bad design, a missing mechanism) and what fixing it trades off; brief one rework for that cause, never one per finding.
- After a rework, check it yourself: read its diff and run the check that shows each blocking finding fixed. Start another review only when the rework changed a contract or a risky area, and give it only that range and the findings it answers.
- At most two review rounds for a task or a lane. After the second, you decide, and carry what remains in your report.
- Report a lane ready only after every review you started on it has come back and you have settled its findings as above.

supervisor.rules:
- Never land a lane while a review of it is still running or its latest findings are unsettled: read status first, and wait for the review.
- A red gate caused only by tests another lane or a known pre-existing failure owns may be landed over, naming those tests; anything else goes back to the Lead.

reviewer.rules: Mark each finding blocking or not. Blocking means behavior wrong, acceptance missed, security weakened, data at risk or a contract broken. Raise a test finding only when a test fails to prove a behavior the acceptance names; do not ask for tests beyond the acceptance. On a second round, read only the range and the findings the brief names.

reviewer-claude.rules: Mark each finding blocking or not. Blocking means behavior wrong, acceptance missed, security weakened, data at risk or a contract broken. Raise a test finding only when a test fails to prove a behavior the acceptance names; do not ask for tests beyond the acceptance. On a second round, read only the range and the findings the brief names.
